details:
Collective Brain is an AI-powered astronaut health intelligence system designed to monitor the wellbeing of an entire crew rather than focusing on individual astronauts separately.

During space missions, astronauts face challenges such as muscle and bone loss, radiation exposure, vision changes, sleep disruption, stress and immune-system changes. These problems can affect not only individuals but also the performance and stability of the entire crew.

Our solution connects different aspects of astronaut health and analyses how they influence one another. It aims to identify patterns, detect potential risks and predict how individual health conditions could affect the crew as a whole. For example, if several astronauts experience stress, exhaustion or isolation at the same time, Collective Brain can identify a possible decline in crew stability and highlight risks to communication and mission efficiency.

The system includes eight specialised features: Muscle Trading Network, Heartbeat Balancer, Crowdsourced Eyes, Mood Gravity, Sleep Orchestra, Immune Shield, Radiation Budget System and Bone Credits System. Each feature focuses on a different astronaut health challenge while contributing information to the overall crew-health picture.

What makes our project unique is its crew-based intelligence approach. Instead of simply displaying separate health measurements, it considers the connections between astronauts and aims to recommend actions such as personalised exercise, workload adjustments, improved sleep schedules and radiation-aware task distribution.

The intended impact is to support healthier astronauts, stronger teamwork, earlier risk identification and safer, more efficient long-duration space missions. In the future, Collective Brain could be developed further with more advanced predictions, improved health-data integration and personalised recommendations.
